newsitem.title: USA: Engineered Support off on backlog-analysts.
newsitem.headline: Engineered Support off on backlog-analysts.

text.p: Engineered Support Systems Inc's stock fell on its lower backlog at the end of the January 31 first quarter, analysts said.
The company's backlog was $76.6 million, compared to $101.6 million a year earlier.

"This is a business where orders come in big chunks," said Huntleigh Securities analyst William Fienup. He said the company's first-quarter earnings of $0.24 a share exceeded his $0.22 a share estimate.

Pauli & Co analyst Vincent Biondo said the lower backlog must be taken in context. The year before, he noted, the company received signiticant orders for air conditioners early rather than later in the year.
Biondo said he was raising his full-year estimate on Engineered Support Systems to $1.15 per share from $1.14 to reflect the company's higher-than-expected first-quarter earnings.
The company makes storage containers, water purification systems, heaters and air conditioners, among other products.
